title: Subaru High-z Exploration of Low-luminosity Quasars (SHELLQs). XIII. Large-scale Feedback and Star Formation in a Low-luminosity Quasar at z = 7.07 on the Local Black Hole to Host Mass Relation
question: What are the star formation, feedback/outflow, gas dynamical, and black hole-host co-evolution properties of the low-luminosity quasar J1243+0100 at z = 7.07?

data.sensitivity: 0.10 mJy beam^-1 per 75 km s^-1 channel ([C II] cube); 13.6 uJy beam^-1 (continuum)

what.value: Optical-to-NIR properties of J1243+0100: z_MgII = 7.07 +/- 0.01, M_1450 = -24.13 +/- 0.08 mag, L_Bol = (1.4 +/- 0.1) x 10^46 erg s^-1, M_BH = (3.3 +/- 2.0) x 10^8 M_sun, lambda_Edd = 0.34 +/- 0.20, C IV blueshift of -2400 km s^-1

evidence.quote: Optical-to-near infrared spectroscopy allowed determination of the redshift ($z_{\rm MgII} = 7.07 \pm 0.01$), UV absolute magnitude ($M_{\rm 1450} = -24.13 \pm 0.08$ mag) and bolometric luminosity ($L_{\rm Bol} = (1.4 \pm 0.1) \times 10^{46}$ erg s$^{-1}$)

what.value: Compilation of properties of z > 7 quasars and z >= 6 HSC and optically luminous quasars for comparison

evidence.quote: As a reference for future higher redshift observations, we summarize the observational properties of the currently known $z > 7$ quasars in Table 5.
Figure 13 shows this relation for $z \gtrsim 6$ quasars using data compiled in (cite: 2019PASJ...71..111I).

recipe.goal: Measure FIR continuum properties in the image and uv planes and derive IR luminosities, dust mass, and SFR
recipe.method: 2D Gaussian fit to continuum map in image plane using CASA imfit; visibility fitting in uv plane with a point source plus extended circular Gaussian after annularly averaging in 20 klambda bins using MIRIAD uvamp; modified blackbody integration with CMB corrections
key_parameters: 20 klambda uv bins; FIR range 42.5-122.5 um; TIR range 8-1000 um
assumptions: Optically thin modified blackbody with T_dust = 47 K, beta = 1.6, kappa_lambda = 0.77 (850 um / lambda)^beta cm^2 g^-1, CMB temperature T_CMB,z = 22.0 K at z = 7.07, Kroupa IMF SFR_TIR = 1.49 x 10^-10 L_TIR / L_sun

recipe.goal: Extract area-integrated [C II] spectrum, fit core and broad wing line profiles, and derive [C II] luminosities, EWs, and SFRs
recipe.method: Integrate cube over +/- 900 km s^-1 to make moment-0 map; extract spectrum within 2 sigma contour of moment-0 map; fit single and concentric double Gaussian profiles to the spectrum
key_parameters: Moment-0 velocity integration range +/- 900 km s^-1; aperture 2 sigma contour of moment-0 map; chi^2 evaluated over +/- 1000 km s^-1; wing center fixed to core center
assumptions: [C II] excited primarily by star formation; De Looze et al. (2014) local H II/starburst calibration log(SFR_[CII]) = -7.06 + 1.0 * log(L_[CII]/L_sun)

recipe.goal: Measure spatial extents of the [C II] core and wing components in image and uv planes
recipe.method: Separate moment-0 maps for core (within 235 km s^-1 FWHM) and wing (+/- 250 to 900 km s^-1); 2D Gaussian fit to core moment-0 with imfit; uv visibility fitting for core (point source + circular Gaussian over 235.270-235.455 GHz) and wing (single circular Gaussian in 50 klambda bins over +/- 250-500 km s^-1 for <300 klambda)
key_parameters: Core frequency range 235.270-235.455 GHz; Wing uv fit frequency ranges 234.970-235.166 GHz and 235.559-235.756 GHz (+/- 250-500 km s^-1), 50 klambda bins, <300 klambda
assumptions: Circular Gaussian geometry for uv visibility models

recipe.goal: Construct velocity moment maps and estimate thin-disk dynamical mass
recipe.method: Create intensity-weighted mean velocity (moment-1) and velocity dispersion (moment-2) maps using CASA immoments with 5 sigma clipping; calculate M_dyn from core deconvolved major axis and FWHM assuming thin rotating disk
key_parameters: 5 sigma clipping threshold in immoments; inclination i = 20.5 deg from axis ratio; D = 1.5 x a_maj; v_circ = 0.75 FWHM / sin(i)
assumptions: Thin rotating disk geometry with inclination determined from deconvolved axis ratio

recipe.goal: Search for companion continuum and [C II] line emitters in the FoV
recipe.method: Search continuum S/N map and [C II] data cube within +/- 1000 km s^-1 across the ~0.13 arcmin^2 FoV above a 5 sigma detection threshold
key_parameters: 5 sigma detection threshold for continuum; >5 sigma peak and >=2 contiguous channels with >3 sigma for line emitters; velocity range +/- 1000 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Calculate neutral atomic and total outflow mass, mass outflow rate, kinetic power, and momentum load
recipe.method: Derive neutral hydrogen outflow mass from broad [C II] wing luminosity in PDR high-density limit; compute outflow rate, kinetic power, and momentum load assuming constant flow
key_parameters: v_out = FWHM_wing / 2 = 499 +/- 113 km s^-1; R_out < 1.3 kpc (half of 3 sigma wing FWHM limit)
assumptions: Constant outflow; high-density limit (n >> n_crit ~ 3 x 10^3 cm^-3); PDR fraction = 0.7; X_C+ = 1.4 x 10^-4; T_ex = 200 K; total multi-phase outflow rate ~3x (~0.5 dex) higher than atomic-only value

recipe.goal: Model 3D gas kinematics of the host galaxy and fit the rotation curve to derive bulge and halo masses
recipe.method: Fit six concentric rings of 0''.1 width to the [C II] data cube using 3DBarolo to extract V_rot and sigma_disp profiles; fit V_rot(r) with a spherical Plummer potential; estimate halo mass from V_rot at scale length
key_parameters: 6 concentric rings with 0''.1 width; 5 sigma clipping; fixed dynamical center to quasar position and V_sys = 0 km s^-1; best-fit i = 25 deg and PA = 87 deg; initial guesses V_rot = 120 km s^-1, sigma_disp = 40 km s^-1, V_rad = 0 km s^-1
assumptions: Concentric tilted rings with uniform inclination and PA; spherical Plummer gravitational potential for bulge; V_rot at scale length (~220 km s^-1) equals halo circular velocity

score_reason: Single ALMA Cycle 7 dataset (2019.1.00074.S) with clear description of calibration/imaging software (CASA 5.6, MIRIAD, 3DBarolo), channel averaging (75 km/s), uv-plane binning and frequency ranges, and explicit equations for all derived physical quantities. rediscovery_reason: Public single-pointing ALMA dataset with straightforward continuum and [C II] line reductions, explicit analytical formulas, and well-defined numeric answer keys for fluxes, sizes, line widths, outflow rate, and dynamical/bulge masses.
